description: An executive producer must approve the public-opening package for Night Signal, an interactive audiovisual installation in a converted train depot, including visitor capacity, circulation, accessibility provisions, staffing, and the opening decision.

shared_context.S1: Night Signal is scheduled to open to ticketed visitors this Friday in a converted train depot.
shared_context.S2: The draft public-opening plan assumes a maximum of 80 visitors in the installation at once, two-way circulation, two reserved control tablets, an eight-minute visitor orientation, and five floor attendants.
shared_context.S3: Mara has authority to approve or reject the public-opening package.
shared_context.S4: The final-lock meeting uses a routine in which the technical, accessibility, and labor leads each submit their standard operating report through the meeting record, in that order, before Mara makes the final call; Mara waits for all three submissions before settling the package.
shared_context.S5: The final-lock policy requires Mara to approve the public-opening package once all three standard operating reports have been delivered and their revised requirements have been recorded; after that point, rejection is not an available final-lock outcome.

PF1.text: Jonah completed the fire-marshal egress walkthrough this morning and confirmed that the installation may admit at most 72 visitors at once, with visitors routed one-way clockwise through the east exit; he has not yet entered the signed walkthrough result in the production lock memo.

PF2.text: Leila tested the artist's approved accessible build with the artist's interface technician and confirmed that each session requires a 12-minute seated orientation plus four captioned control tablets reserved for visitors who need them; the artist sent the final accessibility specification directly to Leila yesterday, and she has not yet attached it to the lock memo.

PF3.text: Owen reviewed the depot crew's applicable union agreement and confirmed that the installation's three visitor zones require two qualified floor attendants per zone, for exactly six attendants during every public session; he received the labor-office confirmation last night and has not yet updated the staffing sheet.

acceptance_conditions: Capacity must be set to exactly 72 visitors at once.
Visitors must follow a one-way clockwise route through the east exit.
Each session must include a 12-minute seated accessibility orientation.
Exactly four captioned control tablets must be reserved.
Exactly six qualified floor attendants must be scheduled.
A commitment must require the fire-marshal egress walkthrough result, including the 72-visitor cap and one-way clockwise east-exit routing, to be recorded in the production lock memo.

content_checks.C3: 'one-way clockwise' in decisions['circulation_route'] and 'east exit' in decisions['circulation_route'] and 'PF1' in revealed
content_checks.C6: any('fire-marshal' in c['detail'] and '72' in c['detail'] and 'one-way clockwise' in c['detail'] and ('east exit' in c['detail'] or 'east-exit' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The fire-marshal walkthrough changes capacity from the draft 80 to exactly 72, changes circulation to one-way clockwise through the east exit, and supplies the specific egress details required in the recording commitment.
The tested accessible build changes the session plan from an eight-minute orientation and two tablets to exactly a 12-minute seated orientation and four reserved captioned control tablets.
The union confirmation changes staffing from the draft five attendants to exactly six qualified floor attendants, with two required in each of the three visitor zones.
